verdict: The system is not a marginal 1.09-profit-factor book that needs broad tightening - that number is an artifact of all five analysts reading the unfiltered replay as if it described the live champion. Re-running the same 1411 rows under the live gate (confidenceThreshold=70, minStrength=MODERATE) gives 487 closed trades, 34.9% win rate, PF 1.33, +108.46R, expectancy +0.223R. What is actually wrong is far more specific and far more fixable: (1) SPX is not underperforming, it is broken - SPX MOMENTUM wins 5.7% of 88 closed trades (-77.10R) while the identical setup returns +0.385R on BTC and +0.487R on Gold, and 48.0% of all SPX trades never resolve versus 17-19% for BTC and Gold; a 5.7% hit rate at median RR 2.0 is a stop/instrument-spec/data defect, not a market verdict, and it costs -32.29R of the live book; (2) BREAKDOWN is being run at the strength where it loses (MODERATE) and gated nowhere, worth -18.82R live, while BREAKDOWN|STRONG is the best bucket in the pack; (3) five setups - RANGE_TRADE_SHORT, RANGE_TRADE_LONG, BUY_OVERSOLD, BREAKOUT, SELL_BOUNCE - have no regime with a usable sample in which they work, and executionDisabledSetups is empty; (4) the adaptation layer is inert and lying - learning.setupStats scores MOMENTUM, the system's only real edge, at 3W/5L and -333.24, the healer reports aiFilter ok=true with 'no trade has been evaluated yet', and 15 journal entries cover 263 sessions. Stack the three real filters and the same history yields 358 closed trades, PF 1.77, +171.08R, expectancy +0.478R: +58% total R and 2.1x per-trade expectancy while keeping 73% of the trade count. Almost every other proposal in the five reports - raising adxTrendingMin, minStrength=STRONG, minEntryRsi, dailyOnlyMinConfidence, cutting maxTradesPerDay, blocking the DAILY+H4_CONFLICT cohort - targets buckets that are either pure SPX contamination or already blocked by the live confidence threshold, and two of them would destroy R outright.

actions.action: Add an asset-scoped execution kill-switch (executionDisabledAssets / tradableAssets, checked in the same pre-open guard as executionDisabledSetups) and disable SPX execution while leaving SPX signal generation on for the paper record.
actions.rationale: Largest single lever and the only one that is a sign flip rather than a degree difference. Under the live gate SPX is 49 closed, WR 12.2%, PF 0.28, -32.29R, expectancy -0.659R, against BTC +29.68R and Gold +111.07R. Removing it alone takes the live book from 487 closed / PF 1.33 / +108.46R to 438 closed / PF 1.49 / +140.75R (+32.29R, expectancy +0.223 -> +0.321) at zero cost to any winning cohort, because SPX has no positive slice: row-level cross-tabs show SPX losing in every cohort, regime, direction and ADX band, and in all eight calendar years (best year 2020 at 5W/15L). It also removes the contamination that is making three other analysts recommend harmful changes.
actions.setting: executionDisabledAssets (does not exist yet; strategySettings only exposes executionDisabledSetups)
actions.measurableWhy: The replay already emits a per-row asset field and generateSignal runs per symbol, so re-running with SPX excluded is a direct filter over replay output - no new instrumentation needed. What the replay cannot verify is that the MT5 bridge honours the new list; that needs a live shadow check.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy (headline proposal) and risk-and-config (proposal 8) both independently rank this first. setup-forensics, strength-gate and regime-fit never examined byAsset at all - a material gap, since it is the biggest number in the pack.
actions.risk: Only 127 of 244 SPX trades resolved, so the true SPX R is unknown and could be worse or better. Cuts diversification from three instruments to two and leaves the book long-only BTC+Gold. Most importantly it masks rather than fixes a probable defect - pair it with action 4 so the kill-switch is a containment measure, not a conclusion.

gate.detail: executionDisabledAssets (does not exist yet; strategySettings only exposes executionDisabledSetups) is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Gate BREAKDOWN to STRONG strength only. Add a per-setup minStrength map consulted at the same point the global minStrength check runs; do not use breakdownEnabled=false and do not add BREAKDOWN to executionDisabledSetups.
actions.rationale: Best R-per-trade-removed after SPX. Under the live gate this is +18.82R for 39 trades removed (+0.483R per removed trade), taking the live book to 448 closed / PF 1.43 / +127.28R. BREAKDOWN|MODERATE is -0.316R expectancy over 145 closed (-45.77R unfiltered, -18.82R live); BREAKDOWN|STRONG is the highest-expectancy bucket in the whole pack at +1.034R over 11 closed, PF 3.71, and is above minSampleForRecommendation. Stacked with action 1 the book reaches 401 closed / PF 1.61 / +157.47R.
actions.setting: per-setup minStrength override (no existing setting expresses this; global minStrength stays MODERATE)
actions.suggestedValues: BREAKDOWN -> STRONG; all other setups -> MODERATE
actions.measurableWhy: Strength is computed inside generateSignal and is present on every replayed row, so a strength-conditional setup gate is fully visible to the existing replay. Re-run and compare setupByStrength directly.
actions.agreement: setup-forensics (proposal 2), strength-gate (proposal 1) and risk-and-config (finding 3) all identify BREAKDOWN|MODERATE as the largest setup-level loss pool. setup-forensics and strength-gate agree on the STRONG carve-out; risk-and-config wants a full disable, which the facts do not support.
actions.risk: The retained slice is 11 closed trades live and only 8 once SPX is removed (+4.83R, WR 50%) - above the minimum sample but thin, so the carve-out is the weakest part of this action. It also cuts roughly 193 of 210 BREAKDOWN signals, removing most short-side participation. If BREAKDOWN|STRONG fails to hold over the next 20 live trades, fall back to a full disable, which still beats the status quo by +7.45R.

gate.detail: per-setup minStrength override (no existing setting expresses this; global minStrength stays MODERATE) is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Populate executionDisabledSetups with the five setups that lose in every regime with a usable sample: RANGE_TRADE_SHORT, RANGE_TRADE_LONG, BUY_OVERSOLD, BREAKOUT, SELL_BOUNCE. Deliberately exclude BUY_DIP and BREAKDOWN from this list.
actions.rationale: A pure settings change, reversible from the dashboard, no new code path. On top of actions 1 and 2 it adds +13.61R and lifts the book to 358 closed, WR 40.8%, PF 1.77, +171.08R, expectancy +0.478R - the full stack is +62.62R over the live baseline, +58% total R and 2.1x expectancy while retaining 73% of trade count. Every one of the five is negative ex-SPX (RANGE_TRADE_SHORT -18.49R, RANGE_TRADE_LONG -11.23R, BUY_OVERSOLD -6.62R, BREAKOUT -5.39R, SELL_BOUNCE -4.88R) and none has a positive regime cell that survives the belowMinSample rule. BUY_DIP is excluded because it is actually positive once SPX is removed (+1.48R over 9 closed) and all three of its regime cells are belowMinSample, so there is no evidence to act on in either direction. This action also subsumes the separate 'raise the bar on SELL signals' proposal: ex-SPX every MOMENTUM and TREND_FOLLOW signal in the pack is a BUY, so the short book is exactly the losing-setup book and a BUY-only filter is numerically identical to gating these setups.
actions.measurableWhy: Setup labels are produced by generateSignal on every replayed bar, so setup-level exclusion is exactly what this replay is built to measure. Re-run and read bySetup.
actions.agreement: All of setup-forensics (proposal 1: this exact five), strength-gate (proposal 2, plus BUY_DIP), regime-fit (proposals 2 and 3, subset) and risk-and-config (proposal 1, plus BREAKDOWN) converge here. Strongest consensus in the pack, and it survives the ex-SPX recheck.
actions.risk: Concentrates the surviving book heavily into MOMENTUM: after actions 1-3, 264 of 358 closed trades and +172.79R of the +171.08R total are MOMENTUM, i.e. everything else nets negative. That is single-setup, long-only, two-asset exposure with no short hedge. If the tape turns to a sustained downtrend the book has no way to participate. Also removes the losing setups' role as a drawdown diversifier, which is untested here.

gate.detail: executionDisabledSetups is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Root-cause the SPX signal pipeline before treating the SPX result as a market fact: audit stop/target distance scaling, symbol point/pip size, contract spec and bar-data integrity for SP500, and check the same code path for BTC and Gold.
actions.rationale: SPX MOMENTUM wins 5.7% of 88 closed trades (PF 0.12, -77.10R) while the identical setup returns +0.385R on BTC and +0.487R on Gold. A 5.7% win rate at a median RR of 2.0 is not an unprofitable strategy - random entry would be near 33% - it is a mechanically wrong stop or price scale. Two more signatures point the same way: 48.0% of SPX trades expire unresolved versus 17.4% BTC and 19.4% Gold, and SPX at adx<20 is 1 win in 52 closed (-50.54R) where BTC+Gold at adx<20 is the single best slice in the book (+125.68R, expectancy +0.467R). Whatever produces that is a defect class that could be silently mis-scaling risk on the profitable instruments too, which is why this outranks the remaining tuning items on risk even though it books no immediate R.
actions.measurableWhy: The replay reproduces the symptom but cannot attribute it: it has no visibility into MT5 symbol specifications, point value, tick size, spread or fill behaviour, and it scores every loss as a flat -1.05R regardless of whether the stop was correctly placed. Diagnosis needs a code and instrument-spec audit plus a bar-data sanity check against a second source, not another replay run.
actions.agreement: loss-autopsy alone hints at it (notes SPX losses have median adx 21.4 / volRatio 0.90 versus 26.2 / 1.25 for wins, and flags 'if the root cause is a data or instrument-spec bug, the ban masks it permanently'). risk-and-config notes the low resolution rate but draws no inference. No analyst compared SPX MOMENTUM against BTC/Gold MOMENTUM, which is where the defect becomes unmistakable.
actions.risk: Diagnostic work that may book no R. The opposite risk is larger: shipping action 1 alone converts a probable bug into a permanent policy, and if the same scaling fault touches BTC or Gold in some regime, the measured +171.08R is overstated by an unknown amount.

actions.action: Re-baseline the fact pack against the live filter: emit every bucket twice, once unfiltered and once restricted to the rows the live champion would actually have taken (currently conf>=70 and minStrength>=MODERATE), and make the live-filtered view the default for any tuning decision.
actions.rationale: This is a process fix that prevents the next four bad decisions. All five analysts quoted PF 1.09 / expectancy 0.064R as the system's condition; the live champion's numbers are PF 1.33 / expectancy +0.223R. The gap is not cosmetic - it inverts specific conclusions. The DAILY+H4_CONFLICT bucket (-30.82R, expectancy -0.734R) that two analysts want gated contains zero trades at conf>=70, so blocking it is worth exactly 0.00R live. The adx20-30 band (-24.6R) that two analysts want to fix with adxTrendingMin is +7.16R live. The conf<50 band (-46.6R) is +3.31R once SPX is removed. Cheap to build: the pack already carries conf and strength on every row.
actions.measurableWhy: confidenceThreshold is precisely what the replay cannot see - generateSignal emits a confidence score but the replay never applies the gate. The fix is to apply the threshold as a post-filter over replay output rather than to teach the replay about it, which is a fact-pack change, not a replay change.
actions.agreement: None of the five. risk-and-config (finding 10) comes closest - it observes that 'more than half the measured pack sits at confidence levels the live threshold would reject, so the headline expectancy is not what this configuration would actually have produced' - then proceeds to argue from the unfiltered numbers anyway, as do the other four.
actions.risk: The live-filtered sample is 487 closed rather than 1081, so per-bucket samples roughly halve and more cells fall below minSampleForRecommendation. Keep both views; use unfiltered for setup-level structure and live-filtered for any settings decision.

actions.action: Rebuild learning.setupStats from the closed-trade history before any adaptation reads it, make the journal and learning writers consume every closed trade, and change the healer so an unexercised gate reports ok=false. Run the aiFilter in log-only shadow mode first.
actions.rationale: The adaptation layer is currently steering against the only thing that works. learning.setupStats scores MOMENTUM at 3W/5L / -333.24 - the setup that is +172.79R and 44.7% WR under the recommended config - and bySymbol.XAUUSD.MOMENTUM at -272.87 against a measured Gold MOMENTUM of +124.23R. It also carries BB_SQUEEZE_WATCH, a setup that appears nowhere in bySetup. Meanwhile healer.checks.aiFilter reports ok=true with detail 'no trade has been evaluated yet - filter unexercised', so a risk gate that has never run is being counted as healthy, and 15 journal entries cover sessionCount 263. Any auto-tuner fed this file will disable MOMENTUM. That is a tail risk large enough to outrank the remaining marginal tuning.
actions.measurableWhy: Entirely outside the replay: these are live persistence, healer and execution-path concerns. Verify by diffing rebuilt setupStats against the fact pack's bySetup and by asserting a non-zero aiFilter evaluation count in the healer.
actions.agreement: risk-and-config alone (findings 1, 4, 5 and proposals 9, 10). strength-gate corroborates the symptom in its finding 7 ('learning.setupStats covers only 4 setups', 'filter unexercised') but proposes no fix. The other three never looked at liveState.
actions.risk: A backfill overwrites live-execution nuance and could abruptly change sizing or setup selection if downstream logic assumes the current small counts or specific setup keys - version the file and diff the resulting decisions first. Flipping unexercised checks to ok=false will turn healer.healthy false and may trigger heal actions that have never once fired (healCount 0), so gate heal actions behind a manual confirm for the first cycle.

actions.action: Restrict SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT to the TRENDING regime, or retire it. Treat this as a trailing cleanup, not a priority.
actions.rationale: It is the only remaining negative setup after actions 1-3: 82 closed ex-SPX, PF 0.91, -5.60R, expectancy -0.068R. Ex-SPX it works only in TRENDING (33 closed, PF 1.17, +3.85R) and loses in RANGING and SQUEEZE (24 closed each, PF 0.78, -4.20R each) - it has no edge in the regime it is named for, where MOMENTUM does the work instead (MOMENTUM|SQUEEZE 64 closed, PF 1.74, +25.8R). Dropping it outright takes the recommended config from 358 closed / PF 1.77 / +171.08R to 276 closed / PF 2.10 / +176.68R, expectancy +0.478 -> +0.640. Small in absolute R, which is why it ranks here.
actions.setting: executionDisabledSetups (retire) or a regime-conditional setup gate (restrict)
actions.suggestedValues: restrict to regime==TRENDING; or add SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT to executionDisabledSetups
actions.measurableWhy: Setup and regime labels are both produced by generateSignal on every replayed bar, so a regime-conditional setup gate is directly measurable via setupByRegime. Note the surviving TRENDING slice depends on adxTrendingMin, which the replay also sees, so both can be swept together.
actions.agreement: setup-forensics (proposal 3) and regime-fit (finding 8) agree on restricting to TRENDING. risk-and-config lists it among the negative setups but does not propose disabling it. SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT|STRONG is belowMinSample (3 closed) and no proposal here rests on it - strength-gate correctly refused to use it.
actions.risk: The surviving TRENDING slice is +0.117R per trade over 33 closed, barely above the 0.05R cost assumption, so restricting rather than retiring may just preserve a break-even setup that adds variance for no return. Retiring removes the last non-MOMENTUM volume and makes the concentration problem in action 3 worse.

gate.detail: executionDisabledSetups (retire) or a regime-conditional setup gate (restrict) is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Do NOT raise confidenceThreshold to 80 on the champion. Run it as a challenger arm only, and judge it on drawdown and position-slot contention rather than total R.
actions.rationale: This is a genuine quality-versus-volume tradeoff that the total-R numbers resolve against. From the live baseline, conf>=80 raises expectancy from +0.223R to +0.333R but cuts total R by -35.59R (268 of 487 trades removed). Applied on top of actions 1-3 it still costs -15.41R (+93.05R over 147 closed at PF 2.08, versus +166.25R over 350 at PF 1.76). Confidence is also not monotonic in the raw pack - conf65-69 (-0.071R) is worse than conf50-64 (+0.061R). The one argument for it is that maxConcurrentPositions=3 makes slots, not signals, the scarce resource, and that is exactly what the replay cannot see - so it must be settled live, on a challenger arm, not decided from these facts.
actions.measurableWhy: Explicitly outside the replay - generateSignal emits confidence but the replay never applies the threshold, and the whole case for raising it rests on position-slot contention enforced by the MT5 bridge (maxConcurrentPositions=3), which the replay also cannot see. The R numbers above come from post-filtering replay output, which measures the signal-quality effect but not the slot-contention effect.
actions.agreement: risk-and-config (proposal 2) proposes 75/80 outright; loss-autopsy proposes a direction-conditional variant (SELL at 80/85). Neither checked the total-R cost. Ranked as a rejection-with-experiment rather than an action because the facts do not support shipping it.
actions.risk: Shipping it to the champion trades away a third of total R for per-trade quality that may not be needed - at roughly 98 live-eligible signals per year (~0.3/day across three assets) against maxTradesPerDay=10, throughput caps are nowhere near binding, so there is currently no scarcity argument. The direction-conditional variant is additionally redundant with action 3.

gate.detail: confidenceThreshold is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

actions.action: Explicitly reject and do not implement: adxTrendingMin 25/30, minStrength=STRONG, minEntryRsi 35/45/50, dailyOnlyMinConfidence 75/80, maxTradesPerDay 10->5, and the DAILY+H4_CONFLICT cohort gate. Leave all six at their current values.
actions.rationale: Each targets a bucket that is either SPX contamination or already blocked live, and two would actively destroy R. adxTrendingMin: the -24.6R adx20-30 band is entirely SPX (SPX adx20-30 -25.06R; BTC+Gold adx20-30 is +0.46R at PF 1.00), and under the live gate all three ADX bands are positive (+96.29R / +7.16R / +5.01R) - there is no negative band to fix, and reclassifying regimes would move trades out of MOMENTUM|TRENDING, the largest profit cell. minStrength=STRONG: costs -87.72R off the live baseline and leaves 50 closed trades across seven years. minEntryRsi: worth +13.52R alone but a near no-op (-1.16R) once the setups are gated, because the low-RSI losses are the short setups - it is a proxy for a filter better applied directly, and a single floor blocks short entries by construction. dailyOnlyMinConfidence: actively harmful - the live DAILY_ONLY_H4_NEUTRAL cohort is 42 closed at PF 2.00 and +0.801R expectancy, the best cohort in the live book, and 100% of it sits in conf 70-79, so a 75/80 floor deletes it. maxTradesPerDay: a no-op at ~0.3 signals/day. Conflict cohort: all 42 rows are conf<70 and are already blocked by the live threshold - worth 0.00R.
actions.measurableWhy: adxTrendingMin is the one tunable the replay sees directly and is the only entry in autoTunableSettings, so a 20/25/30 sweep is cheap and should be run once to confirm the rejection rather than assumed. minEntryRsi and minStrength are also visible to generateSignal and can be swept. dailyOnlyMinConfidence, the conflict-cohort gate and maxTradesPerDay are not measurable - they live in generateSignalMTF and the MT5 bridge respectively.
actions.agreement: This action contradicts regime-fit (proposals 4, 5), risk-and-config (proposals 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9) and loss-autopsy (proposal 2). It is backed by loss-autopsy's finding 5, which correctly identified ADX 20-30 as SPX contamination and warned it must not be filtered on, and by setup-forensics (finding 8) and strength-gate (proposal 1), which both correctly rejected a global STRONG gate.
actions.risk: Holding adxTrendingMin at its default leaves the only auto-tunable setting untested and healCount at 0 - if the auto-tuner is silently unable to write the value, that stays hidden. Run the 20/25/30 sweep once to verify both the rejection and that the tuner can actually move the setting.

gate.detail: adxTrendingMin, minStrength, minEntryRsi, dailyOnlyMinConfidence, maxTradesPerDay is outside what the replay can see (adxTrendingMin) — needs a human decision

blindSpots: Unresolved trades are silently dropped. 330 of 1411 rows (23.4%) are EXPIRED and contribute nothing to any R figure. The rate is wildly uneven - 48.0% for SPX versus 17.4% BTC and 19.4% Gold - so roughly half the SPX record is unscored and the SPX verdict rests on the resolved half. Nothing in the pack says whether an expired trade would have been a win, a loss, or a manual close, and nothing says what the live system does with a position that never reaches TP or SL.

The R model is an idealisation. Every loss is scored at exactly -1.05R and every win at rr-0.05, with a flat costAssumptionR of 0.05 standing in for all spread, slippage, swap and commission. There is no gap risk, no partial fill, no stop-hunt, no weekend gap and no variable spread. Gold and SPX in particular have session-dependent spreads that a flat 0.05R will understate. The measured +0.478R expectancy is therefore an upper bound.

No equity path, so no drawdown, no risk of ruin, no correlation. With riskPercent=0.15 and the recommended config being long-only BTC and Gold, the two instruments will draw down together in a dollar-liquidity shock, and nothing here measures that. Total R and profit factor say nothing about the maximum peak-to-trough the account would have suffered, which is the number that actually determines whether this configuration is survivable.

Sequencing and slot contention are invisible. The replay treats every signal as independently takeable; live, maxConcurrentPositions=3 means simultaneous signals compete for slots and some are simply never opened. Which one wins the slot is unmodelled. This is precisely the mechanism that would justify raising confidenceThreshold, so the strongest argument for action 8 is also the one these facts cannot evaluate.

The replay may not be the live signal path. It runs generateSignal; live execution runs generateSignalMTF. The cohort labels (H4_ONLY, DAILY+H4_AGREE, DAILY+H4_CONFLICT, DAILY_ONLY_H4_NEUTRAL) are the replay's own reconstruction of multi-timeframe agreement, and nothing here verifies that the live MTF path produces the same distribution - or the same signals at all. Every cohort-based conclusion is conditional on that unverified equivalence.

Everything is in-sample. All nine actions are being fitted to the same 2019-2026 bars that produced the facts, with no holdout, no walk-forward and no out-of-sample confirmation. The recommended config keeps 358 of 1081 closed rows; selecting three filters against one history and reporting the surviving subset's PF is exactly the procedure that manufactures overfitting. The +171.08R figure should be treated as a ceiling, not a forecast.

The only real-money evidence is 13 trades and it disagrees. liveState.learning holds 5 wins and 8 losses across 4 setups with MOMENTUM at 3W/5L and -333.24 currency, and journalEntries is 15 against sessionCount 263. That sample is far too small to overturn 1081 replayed trades, but it is also the only observation of actual fills, actual spreads and actual bridge behaviour in the entire pack - and it points the other way. Nothing here reconciles the two.

Regime and trend labels are the system's own output, not ground truth. MOMENTUM fires exclusively under a STRONG UPTREND label, so 'MOMENTUM works' and 'the classifier's STRONG UPTREND label is informative' cannot be separated with these facts. If the classifier is mislabelling, the error is invisible to every bucket in the pack because every bucket is cut by the same labels.

No sizing or currency dimension. riskPercent is 0.15 against a default of 1, fixedLotSize is 0 and maxLotSize is 10, but nothing maps R to account currency or verifies that a 1R loss is actually 0.15% of equity on each instrument. The live learning file's -333.24 on MOMENTUM against a measured +155.26R is the visible symptom of that gap being unreconciled.

Nothing measures why SPX fails. The 5.7% MOMENTUM win rate and 48% expiry rate identify a defect but the pack contains no bar-level price data, no stop distances, no instrument specifications and no fill records - so the facts can localise the problem to SPX and rule out regime, cohort, direction and indicator band as explanations, but cannot name the cause. Action 4 has to be answered outside this dataset.
